headline: CHINA RARE EARTH LOCKDOWN: New Controls Restrict Trace-Content Products — F-35 and Missile Supply Chains at Risk
snippet: China has imposed its most stringent rare earth and magnet export controls yet, for the first time applying the foreign direct product rule to restrict items containing even trace amounts of Chinese-sourced material. U.S. yttrium imports from China collapsed 95% under the new regime — from 333 tonnes in the eight months before restrictions to just 17 tonnes after — putting F-35, Tomahawk missile, and radar manufacturing supply chains at direct risk.

headline: GEOPOLITICAL LOTTERY TICKET? Analyst Stress-Tests a Western Critical Metals Play Amid China's Rare Earth War
snippet: With China weaponizing rare earth exports and Trump's 'Project Vault' earmarking $12B for a U.S. critical mineral strategic reserve, a Motley Fool analyst asks whether geopolitical tailwinds justify current valuations in Western critical metals stocks — or whether retail investors are paying a Trump premium for sector risks they've seen before. The conclusion: real exposure to genuine supply-chain demand, but position size accordingly.

headline: NGEx HITS 207 g/t GOLD OVER 17 METRES at Lunahuasi — Two Bonanza Intervals Sit 660m Apart in Argentina
snippet: NGEx Minerals (TSX: NGEX) reported extraordinary Phase 4 results at its Lunahuasi copper-gold-silver project in San Juan, Argentina: hole DPDH070 intersected 17.3m at 207.79 g/t Au including a 2m bonanza grading 1,740 g/t Au. A second bonanza zone sits 660m away, confirming the system's scale; Phase 4 is now complete at 27,318m drilled across 32 holes, with Phase 5 planning underway.

headline: NEW ZONE UNLOCKED at Historic Hemlo Mine: 16.1 g/t Au Over 8.1m in Newly Defined South-Rim — All 7 Holes Hit
snippet: Hemlo Mining (TSXV: HMMC) has defined a new high-grade domain immediately adjacent to its active C-Zone at the historic Hemlo gold mine in Ontario, with first holes returning 16.1 g/t Au over 8.1m and a bonanza intercept of 59.7 g/t Au over 2m. Every one of the initial seven South-Rim holes hit mineralization; the company is only 20% through its 130,000m 2026 exploration program.

headline: USA RARE EARTH UP 114% YTD as Q1 Shows First Commercial Yttrium Output and $2.8B Brazil Deal
snippet: USA Rare Earth (NASDAQ: USAR) reported Q1 milestones including first commercial yttrium production at its LCM facility, commissioning of Stillwater Phase 1a, and a $2.8B acquisition of Serra Verde in Brazil — while shares surged 114.71% year-to-date to a $5.68B market cap. With China exporting just 17 tonnes of yttrium to the U.S. this year, USAR has become the benchmark stock for domestic rare earth supply chain exposure.

headline: URANIUM HOLDS $86/LB as Meta's 7.8GW Nuclear Contract and AI Data Center Boom Reshape Demand Outlook
snippet: Uranium spot held near $86–87/lb this week, near a two-month high, as AI-driven nuclear demand forced a structural reassessment: Meta contracted 7.8GW of dedicated nuclear capacity and Microsoft locked in 800MW for AI data centres. With Kazatomprom having cut its 2026 output target by roughly 8 million pounds (5% of global primary supply), analysts project utility re-contracting could push prices toward $100–$120/lb.

headline: COPPER SLIDES TO $6.25/LB on Hot CPI Data; Grasberg Full Restart Now Pushed to Early 2028
snippet: Copper futures fell to $6.25/lb — a second straight session of losses — as hotter-than-expected U.S. inflation reignited rate-hike bets and drove profit-taking from near-record highs. Supply-side relief remains distant: PT Freeport Indonesia confirmed the Grasberg mine full-restart has been pushed to early 2028 from end-2027, leaving the world's second-largest copper mine operating at 40–50% capacity after September's fatal mudslide.

headline: BARRICK EARNINGS UP 256%, Launches $3B Buyback as Gold at $4,500+ Turns Miners Into Cash Machines
snippet: Barrick Mining posted Q1 2026 adjusted EPS of $0.98 (up 180% YoY), beat revenue estimates by $380M, and approved a $3B share buyback — while gold output of 719,000 oz topped its own 640,000–680,000 oz guidance range. Agnico Eagle, Kinross Gold, and AngloGold Ashanti also reported record quarterly free cash flows, together returning over $1B to shareholders in a quarter that signals gold miners are finally translating $4,500+ gold into balance-sheet strength.

headline: SIGMA LITHIUM FINED by Brazil Labor Inspectors for Using Waste Pile Under Active Shutdown Order
snippet: Brazilian labor inspectors fined Sigma Lithium (NASDAQ: SGML) after finding trucks actively depositing waste into a pile that had been formally shut down since December 2025 due to a partial fracture near a local school. Inspectors cited two violations: continued use of the banned pile and denial of mandatory site access. The incident adds to operational and reputational pressure on one of Brazil's most closely watched lithium producers.

headline: NdPr OXIDE DROPS 21% IN APRIL to $99.61/kg — Sharpest Monthly Fall Since Rally Began, But 88% Up YTD
snippet: Neodymium-praseodymium oxide fell 21% in April to $99.61/kg — its steepest monthly decline since the Q1 bull run began — as Chinese traders took profits and downstream consumers drew down over-bought inventory. Despite the correction, NdPr is still 88% above its January open and above the cost base of major Western producers; analysts see $95–$115/kg as a consolidation range ahead of China's mid-year 2026 mining quota announcement in June.
